metadata.title: Best Punjabi Summer Home Cooked Food with MamaKTreats I Phalsa Sharbat, Bhindi Raita, Aamras Poori
metadata.description:
Our next episode of Delhi Community Food Stories takes us into the welcoming kitchen of Kanan Bala ji, a passionate home chef who shares a glimpse of her everyday Punjabi summer meal — a celebration of seasonal produce, light cooking, and heartfelt hospitality.

We began with tori-kakdi ki sabzi, a humble preparation using ridge gourd and cucumber — vegetables that are in season and known for their cooling properties. Cooked with minimal spices and just a touch of oil, the dish had a comforting, runny gravy — perfect for hot summer days.

Next, Kanan ji prepared bharwan tinde, a North Indian classic where round gourd is gently stuffed with a simple spice blend and lightly sautéed in oil. It’s a dish that appears regularly on her table during the season — subtle in flavour, yet full of homey goodness.

She then introduced us to a fiery raw mango chutney — a condiment made with raw mangoes, tomatoes, garlic, and green chillies. Tangy, spicy, and utterly addictive, it’s a staple in her home that brings a zing to every bite.

Her daughter, Kishi, joined us next to make falsa ka sharbat, a cooling summer drink. With just a few steps and a splash of soda for fizz, she whipped up a refreshing concoction that she loves sipping with her meals.

As the food was laid out, we sat down to eat together. Kanan ji served us with immense love — each bite a reflection of her warmth, her rootedness, and her deep connection to the food she makes.

After the meal, we visited Kishi’s lush organic terrace garden. She walked us through the vibrant green space that she’s nurtured with her own hands — a haven that supplies much of what goes into their meals. From seasonal greens to herbs and even composting setups, her commitment to mindful living was inspiring.

Back in the kitchen, we ended on a sweet note with aamras, made from ripe Alphonso mangoes. Kanan ji carefully extracted the pulp, blended it smooth, and flavored it with saffron and cardamom. Served with bite-sized puris, it was pure, velvety indulgence.

This episode is a gentle ode to seasonal home cooking, where everyday ingredients turn into something truly special. It reflects the warmth of family traditions, the joy of sharing meals, and the quiet strength of women who keep these culinary legacies alive.
